intro_html: Turns "who has the projector?" from a question nobody can answer into a register anybody can read — every laptop, vehicle key and access card you hand out, recorded, approved, chased when it comes back late, and backed by a document the person actually signed.

features.title: One Register For What You Lend
features.desc: Laptops, phones, vehicle keys, access cards, instruments — each with its own description, photo and company, and an optional link to a catalogue product.

features.title: Request, Approve, Return
features.desc: A request is raised as a draft, sent for approval, approved or refused by an HR officer, then closed when the item comes back.

features.title: A Handover Document They Sign
features.desc: One printable page carrying the holder, the item and its description, the reason, the return date, an undertaking and two signature lines.

features.title: The Same Item Is Never Promised Twice
features.desc: Approving an item somebody already holds is refused outright, and the message names who holds it and under which request.

features.title: Overdue Returns Chase Themselves
features.desc: A daily job emails the holder from the day before the return date onwards, and a manager can send a reminder by hand at any time.

features.title: Extensions And Refusals Stay On Record
features.desc: A refusal must carry a written reason. An extension records the new date without destroying the one originally promised.

features.title: Every Employee's Holdings, One Click
features.desc: Two counters on the employee form: everything that person has ever held, and what they are holding right now.

features.title: Analysis By Item, Person Or Status
features.desc: A pivot over the register showing what gets requested most, who tends to run late, and what is approved against what is refused.

limitations: No quantities or stock integration. One register row is one physical item; the optional product link is descriptive and moves nothing in Inventory.
No condition, damage or maintenance tracking, and no repair workflow.
No financial value, depreciation or insurance fields.
No multi-level approval. One officer approval is final.
No escalation. Reminders go to the holder only, never to a manager.
No barcode scanning, and no on-screen signature capture — the handover document is printed and signed on paper.
No per-item history model. The request records are the history.
The reminder schedule is fixed at daily 05:00, with no settings screen.
Overdue status is calculated rather than stored, so it cannot be grouped on directly. Use the Overdue search filter.
Regular employees cannot delete their own requests. An HR Administrator removes a mistaken record.
